method: The u04 exemplar and its five review rounds (a1.1-u04.r1–r5) and the u01 r1 review were read first, and every finding class they raised was checked here; recurrences are named in the findings and in notes. Both reviewers read every German string of the unit: title and title.canDo, spec.situation and the lexicon block titles, the Folge (10 lines) and its gist item, the three inputs (LS1 and LS2 video-call dialogues, 10 lines each; LS3 classroom scene, 10 lines, plus Emre's chat post), the two exam texts, the strategy card, 8 redemittel, the Sp2 task (situation, instructions, openingLine, aiRole, cards, 8 hintWords, 10 model turns), the S2 task (situation, taskDe, 3 Leitpunkte with cues, checklist, model text), the 3 check lines, story beat and cliffhanger, every endLine and explanation.de, the 32 u03 entries of a1.1/lexicon.json and the rule cards rc.possessiv-mein-dein and rc.vokalwechsel that the unit shows. We solved every item blind from promptDe plus its options, tiles or audio line only: 1 start gist, 15 input items, 12 structuredInput, 33 authored pool items, 12 reserve items, 5 exam items, 8 check items and 2 proof items (88 items; every key is right). For sentence_building we permuted the tiles and checked each V2, V1 and declarative-question order against accepted[] and the Aussagesatz / Frage / W-Frage frame; typed answers were graded by running src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js itself on candidate answers (results quoted in F02, F03). Generators were traced: 3 × dictation.fromInput (6 source lines, none with `say`), numbers.dictation, 3 × lex.articlePlural and 2 × lex.glossTyped (all sources productive, all plurals regular), 3 × lex.glossMatch, perception.intonation and perception.pairs. Non-exam three-option key positions were counted (10 a / 11 b / 14 c over 35 keys; the u04 r4-F03 class does not recur). The exam block was checked against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json (l1: 5 × richtig_falsch, 2 options, two texts of 56–92 words; sp2: cards-ask, 2 rounds, 0 min preparation; s2: 3 Leitpunkte, about 30 words, Anrede/Gruß not a Leitpunkt) and against the rubrics speaking/sd1-sp2.json and writing/sd1-s2.json and the grader (netlify/functions/_shared/rubrics/grade.mjs criteriaPlan, buildSpeakingUserPrompt). Word counts were recomputed with the validator's wordCount: t1 69, t2 69, LS3 chat 43, Folge 88, LS1/LS2/LS3 dialogues 129/130/133, S2 model 28, cliffhanger 20. Before the LEX-01 surface walk landed, we ran the validator's own knownForms + licensedForms and LEX-01's coverage() at a1.1-u03 over every German string of the unit and looked up each unknown token's allocation in all eight lexicons; after it landed we sorted its findings at two snapshots, 57 blockers at 22:09 and 10 at 22:14 (F01). The grammar ceiling was read against grammar-spine.json (g.possessiv-mein-dein and g.vokalwechsel u03; g.ja-nein-frage and g.praesens u01–u02; g.artikel-genus-plural u04; g.akkusativ u06, chunk u04; g.praep-dativ chunk u05; g.muessen-duerfen-man chunk u08; g.possessiv-sein-ihr a1.2-u03) and against curriculum/a1-1.md §6 U3 and decision D7. New-word load was checked against level-profiles.json (a1.1: 24–32 new, productive share 0.5; u03: 32 entries, 15 productive). Can-dos were read against registries/cando/a1.json; the cast against casts/series.json and casts/a1.json (age, origin, languages, residence, relations and du/Sie, voices); story continuity against u01, u02 (the cliffhanger „Auch Nair? Wer ist das, Frau Nair?“), u04, u05 and u08. The learner-facing rendering of title.canDo, speaking and writing task texts was confirmed in src/components/course-v2 (StartView l. 84, SpeakingTaskView l. 23–24, WritingTaskView l. 316–320: German only). verdict: Not exit-ready: 1 BLOCKER, 5 MAJOR, 10 MINOR. The unit is well built. The story picks up u02's cliffhanger word for word and runs through a believable day: the Anmeldung, the video call with Olena, Arjun's surprise entrance, the classroom scene with Emre online. The scenes are lively (Bilal's mother asking about a girlfriend, Olena's „Mütter sind so!“, the nephew who always sleeps). Every cast fact agrees with the bible and with u01, u02, u04, u05 and u08. du/Sie is right in every exchange. All 88 keys are right, the dictations match their audio, number words are accepted, and the Lesen Teil 1 block is exact to sd1.json and original. What stops exit: (1) the LEX-01 surface walk, which landed during this round, still fails the unit with 10 blockers after its allowlist grew: 7 are the unit's own later-unit words on German-only task screens (all three S2 Leitpunkte and the checklist are built on „Personen“, u10), and 3 are tokenizer and name gaps for the rail owner (F01); (2) three „Bilden Sie die Frage.“ items grade WRONG the declarative question („Das ist dein Bruder?“) that the same Lernschritt's Aussprache drill teaches as a question (F02); (3) the bare „Korrigieren Sie: „Er sprecht gut Deutsch.““ rejects „Ihr sprecht gut Deutsch.“, the u04 r5-F01 class back because its rail was never written (F03); (4) cd.a1.personen-beschreiben is claimed, but no spoken task asks for an age or a job (F04); (5) the unit's Partner word card says Sophie lives in Dresden with her partner, against the cast bible, u02 and u05 (F05); (6) lesen and schlafen carry the unit's productive Vokalwechsel drill but are receptive in the lexicon (F06). F04 and F06 are the u04/u01 classes that reach their third A1.1 unit here, so under §9.4 they are stop-the-line classes. The minors are mostly one-line data edits.

Smaller breaks: spec.cast is incomplete, a listed text type is not in the unit, Bilal writes „Das sind …“ without a photo, and Emre's wife is unnamed here but introduced as news in u08 (F11).
scoreNotes.E: Instructions are ≤ 90 characters, every Lernschritt opens with an easy gist item, and every endLine names the win. It scores 3 because the two Aufgaben's German-only instruction screens are hard for this learner to read. The S2 Leitpunkte and checklist are built on „Personen“ (u10) and open with „Nennen Sie“, and the Sp2 situation runs to 54 words (F01). No 360 px walkthrough was run.

findings.problem: The German prompt asks only for 'die Frage'. In the same Lernschritt, the Aussprache drill teaches that „Das ist dein Bruder?“ (statement word order with rising intonation) is a question, and its focus line files it under „Ja/Nein-Frage steigend“. A learner who applies the drill builds „Das ist dein Bruder?“. That is correct spoken German (an Intonationsfrage), yet it is graded WRONG: check.js folds the '?', and the string then equals the statement. ls3-p05 matches the drill's own pair („Sie ist verheiratet?“ → „Du bist verheiratet?“), and „Du schläfst schon?“ is the everyday surprised question. ls1-p08 accepts the marked order „Ist dein Bruder das?“ but rejects the much more common declarative question, so marked orders are treated unevenly. Only promptEn ('Build the yes/no question') and the u02 rule card rc.ja-nein-frage (verb in position 1) tie the key to V1, and ITM-01 forbids the English gloss as the only cue. Because punctuation is folded, the checker can never accept the declarative question without also accepting the statement, so the fix has to go into the prompt.
findings.fix: promptDe on all three items: „Bilden Sie die Ja/Nein-Frage (Verb auf Position 1).“ (51 characters; the keys do not change). Keep the perception drill, but let its focus say what it trains: „Satzmelodie: Frage steigend ↗ (auch „Das ist dein Bruder?“), Aussage und W-Frage fallend ↘“. Optionally drop „Ist dein Bruder das?“ from ls1-p08, so that the two marked orders are treated alike (as in u04 r2-F02).
findings.proposedRule: ITM-09/ITM-01: a sentence_building item whose key is a V1 question (finite verb first, answer ends in '?') must name the verb position in promptDe („Ja/Nein-Frage“ plus „Position 1“ or „Verb vorn“), because check.js folds '?' and the declarative permutation of the same tiles can always be built. Failing fixture: a1.1-u03 ls1-p08 with „Bilden Sie die Frage.“. The test runs over all registered courses.
